title: Liver as food
lead:
{{Short description|Liver meat used as food}}
[[File:Pig's liver with sauteed onion.jpg|thumb|Slice of pig's [[liver and onions]] ]]
[[File:Cornmeal mush liver.jpg|thumb|[[Mămăligă]] ([[cornmeal]] mush) with chicken liver, cuisine of [[Moldovan cuisine|Moldova]]]]
[[File:Russian Cod liver in an opened can.jpg|thumb|Canned cod liver (see also: [[cod liver oil]])]]

The '''liver''' of mammals, [[fowl]], and fish is commonly eaten as food by humans (see [[offal]]). [[Pork]], [[Lamb and mutton|lamb]], [[veal]], [[beef]], chicken, [[Goose as food|goose]], and [[Cod as food|cod]] [[liver]]s are widely available from butchers and supermarkets while [[common stingray|stingray]] and [[burbot]] livers are common in some European countries.
